1"""poisson candidate v3: two independent philox chains per Knuth chunk. 

2 

3Successor of the v2 kernel (block-max Knuth bound, 4 uniforms per philox 

4call, uint32 counters). v3 keeps the sampler contract -- per-element philox 

5streams with ``STRIDE``-spaced counters, truncation probability <= 1e-5 on the 

6small path -- and spends the same op budget more efficiently: 

7 

8* uniforms come from the top 24 bits of the philox word (``(r >> 8) * 2**-24``). 

9 Three cheap vector ops replace the five-op ``uint_to_uniform_float`` chain 

10 (bitcast + where + mul); 24 random mantissa bits are plenty for a product of 

11 at most 16 uniforms and the distribution stays exactly uniform on 

12 ``[0, 1)``. Only the drawn values change, not the distribution; 

13* the ``max(u, 1e-10)`` clamp is gone. If u == 0 then p == 0 <= L and k 

14 freezes -- which is precisely the Knuth semantics. The clamp only made a 

15 difference for lam > 23 *and* u == 0 (probability ~1e-9), so results are 

16 unchanged for every realistic input; 

17* the loop bound is capped at the small-path ceiling ``min(bmax, 30)`` before 

18 the 3-sigma margin. Lanes with lam > 30 discard their Knuth result in 

19 favour of the normal approximation anyway, so the loop only has to cover 

20 lanes that actually read it (nit 17 -> 13 for an all-lam-50 block); 

21* the loop processes two philox calls per iteration (8 uniforms). The two 

22 chains depend only on their own counters, so the compiler can overlap them, 

23 and the consumption order is unchanged, so k is bit-identical to the 

24 sequential loop. Over-drawing to a multiple of 8 is safe: p is monotone 

25 non-increasing, so once p <= L no later uniform can bump k. Every element 

26 owns a 64-counter slot (``STRIDE``), and the widened loop consumes at most 

27 ``2 * ceil(17 / 2) + 1 = 19 < 64`` counters of it; 

28* one BLOCK bucket for every dtype: 512 for N <= 16384 and 4096 above. The 

29 16-bit-specific 2048 bucket from v2 is gone -- with the 24-bit conversion 

30 the fp16/bf16 widen hazard no longer penalises 4096, and 4096 is faster 

31 across the board (1M fp16: 78.9 -> 66.4 us); 

32* the grid must be SIP-aligned. 24 CTAs on 24 SIPs beat 48 (one program per 

33 SIP gets the full DSM) and beat raw intermediate counts badly: 32 CTAs on 

34 24 SIPs leaves 8 SIPs with two programs and 16 with one, which measured 

35 ~97 us vs ~67 us at 1M fp32. The launcher therefore uses ``cdiv`` when it 

36 fits on one CTA per SIP and clamps to ``NUM_SIPS`` otherwise. 

37 

38Measured (op-level do_bench median, warmup 1000ms / rep 100ms, gcu400): 

39 

40 fp32 1M 74.2 -> 67.7 us (u24+noclamp+g24) 

41 fp16 1M 87.1 -> 66.4 us (BLOCK 2048 -> 4096 dominates) 

42 bf16 1M 66.7 us 

43 fp32 65K 9.1 -> 8.8 us 

44 fp16 65K 12.2 -> 8.7 us (BLOCK 2048 g32 -> 4096 g16) 

45 fp32 4K 4.8 -> 4.8 us (launch bound) 

46 

47The 64-bit-counter (WIDE) path, the increment accounting and the normal 

48approximation for lam > 30 are unchanged from v2; the normal approximation 

49now also draws 24-bit uniforms, which the mean/variance tolerance swallows. 

50""" 

51 

52import logging 

53 

54import torch 

55import triton 

56import triton.language as tl 

57 

58from flag_gems.runtime import torch_device_fn 

59from flag_gems.runtime.backend._enflame.gcu400.ops.poisson import NUM_SIPS 

60from flag_gems.utils import libentry 

61from flag_gems.utils.random_utils import philox_backend_seed_offset 

62from flag_gems.utils.shape_utils import volume 

63 

64logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

65 

66__all__ = ["poisson"] 

67 

68_BLOCK_SMALL = 512 

69_BLOCK_LARGE = 4096 

70_SMALL_N = 16384 

71_LAMBDA_THRESHOLD = 30.0 

72# Cap on uniforms per element (hard limit of the Knuth loop). lam < 30 needs 

73# at most ~49 uniforms, so the cap never binds on the small-lambda path. 

74_MAX_UNIFORMS = 64 

75_PHILOX_STRIDE = 64 

76# off * STRIDE must stay inside uint32 for the fast counter path. 

77_U32_COUNTER_MAX_ELEMS = 2**32 // _PHILOX_STRIDE 

78 

79 

80@triton.jit 

81def _u24(r): 

82 """Uniform float in [0, 1): top 24 bits of a philox word.""" 

83 return (r >> 8).to(tl.float32) * 5.960464477539063e-08 

84 

85 

86@triton.jit 

87def _poisson_large(lam, seed, c0, c1, z): 

88 """Normal approximation (Box-Muller), used only for lam > threshold.""" 

89 r0, r1, r2, r3 = tl.philox(seed, c0, c1, z, z) 

90 u1 = tl.maximum(_u24(r0), 1e-10) 

91 u2 = _u24(r1) 

92 two_pi = 6.283185307179586 

93 radius = tl.sqrt(-2.0 * tl.log(u1)) 

94 result = lam + tl.sqrt(lam) * (radius * tl.cos(two_pi * u2)) 

95 return tl.floor(tl.maximum(result, 0.0) + 0.5) 

96 

97 

98@libentry() 

99@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["philox_seed", "philox_offset", "N"]) 

100def poisson_kernel_dyn( 

101 inp_ptr, 

102 out_ptr, 

103 N, 

104 philox_seed, 

105 philox_offset, 

106 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

107 LAMBDA_THRESHOLD: tl.constexpr, 

108 MAX_UNIFORMS: tl.constexpr, 

109 STRIDE: tl.constexpr, 

110 WIDE: tl.constexpr, 

111): 

112 seed = philox_seed.to(tl.int64) 

113 philox_offset = philox_offset.to(tl.int64) 

114 c0_base = (philox_offset & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32) 

115 c1 = ((philox_offset >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32) 

116 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

117 npid = tl.num_programs(0) 

118 ar = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

119 for blk in tl.range(pid, (N + BLOCK - 1) // BLOCK, npid): 

120 off = blk * BLOCK + ar 

121 mask = off < N 

122 lam = tl.maximum( 

123 tl.load(inp_ptr + off, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32), 0.0 

124 ) 

125 bmax = tl.max(lam) 

126 # Knuth needs N ~ 1 + Poisson(lam) uniforms; three sigma covers the 

127 # tail. Lanes above the threshold never read their Knuth result, so 

128 # the bound only has to cover the small-path ceiling of the block max. 

129 bl = tl.minimum(bmax, LAMBDA_THRESHOLD * 1.0) 

130 need = tl.minimum(bl + 3.0 * tl.sqrt(bl) + 3.0, MAX_UNIFORMS * 1.0) 

131 nit = (need * 0.25).to(tl.int32) + 1 

132 n2 = (nit + 1) // 2 

133 

134 if WIDE: 

135 counter = c0_base.to(tl.int64) + off.to(tl.int64) * STRIDE 

136 c0 = (counter & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32) 

137 c1v = ((counter >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32) 

138 else: 

139 # uint32 keeps the per-element counter arithmetic off the (emulated) 

140 # int64 path; off * STRIDE cannot wrap because WIDE is False. 

141 c0 = c0_base + off.to(tl.uint32) * STRIDE 

142 c1v = c1 

143 z = c0 * 0 

144 

145 L = tl.exp(-lam) 

146 p = lam * 0.0 + 1.0 

147 k = (lam * 0).to(tl.int32) 

148 for _ in tl.range(0, n2): 

149 # Two independent philox chains, consumed in stream order, so k 

150 # is bit-identical to the sequential loop. Over-draw to a 

151 # multiple of 8 uniforms is safe: p is monotone non-increasing, 

152 # once p <= L no later uniform can raise k. 

153 ra0, ra1, ra2, ra3 = tl.philox(seed, c0, c1v, z, z) 

154 rb0, rb1, rb2, rb3 = tl.philox(seed, c0 + 1, c1v, z, z) 

155 c0 = c0 + 2 

156 pp = p * _u24(ra0) 

157 k = tl.where(pp > L, k + 1, k) 

158 p = pp 

159 pp = p * _u24(ra1) 

160 k = tl.where(pp > L, k + 1, k) 

161 p = pp 

162 pp = p * _u24(ra2) 

163 k = tl.where(pp > L, k + 1, k) 

164 p = pp 

165 pp = p * _u24(ra3) 

166 k = tl.where(pp > L, k + 1, k) 

167 p = pp 

168 pp = p * _u24(rb0) 

169 k = tl.where(pp > L, k + 1, k) 

170 p = pp 

171 pp = p * _u24(rb1) 

172 k = tl.where(pp > L, k + 1, k) 

173 p = pp 

174 pp = p * _u24(rb2) 

175 k = tl.where(pp > L, k + 1, k) 

176 p = pp 

177 pp = p * _u24(rb3) 

178 k = tl.where(pp > L, k + 1, k) 

179 p = pp 

180 

181 result = k.to(tl.float32) 

182 if bmax > LAMBDA_THRESHOLD: 

183 large = _poisson_large(lam, seed, c0, c1v, z) 

184 result = tl.where(lam <= LAMBDA_THRESHOLD, result, large) 

185 tl.store(out_ptr + off, result, mask=mask) 

186 

187 

188def poisson(input, generator=None): 

189 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME POISSON") 

190 assert input.dtype in ( 

191 torch.float16, 

192 torch.bfloat16, 

193 torch.float32, 

194 torch.float64, 

195 ), f"Unsupported dtype: {input.dtype}" 

196 

197 inp = input.contiguous() 

198 N = volume(inp.shape) 

199 out = torch.empty_like(inp) 

200 if N == 0: 

201 return out 

202 

203 block = _BLOCK_SMALL if N <= _SMALL_N else _BLOCK_LARGE 

204 cdiv = (N + block - 1) // block 

205 # GCU400 wants SIP-aligned grids: one program per SIP beats two, and 

206 # intermediate counts leave some SIPs with two programs and others with 

207 # one (~45% slower at 1M fp32). Small launches fit inside NUM_SIPS. 

208 grid = cdiv if cdiv <= NUM_SIPS else NUM_SIPS 

209 increment = triton.cdiv(N * _PHILOX_STRIDE, 4) 

210 philox_seed, philox_offset = philox_backend_seed_offset( 

211 increment, generator=generator 

212 ) 

213 with torch_device_fn.device(inp.device): 

214 poisson_kernel_dyn[(grid,)]( 

215 inp, 

216 out, 

217 N, 

218 philox_seed, 

219 philox_offset, 

220 BLOCK=block, 

221 LAMBDA_THRESHOLD=_LAMBDA_THRESHOLD, 

222 MAX_UNIFORMS=_MAX_UNIFORMS, 

223 STRIDE=_PHILOX_STRIDE, 

224 WIDE=N > _U32_COUNTER_MAX_ELEMS, 

225 num_warps=4, 

226 ) 

227 return out
